intent: One choosable option in a Combobox's list, identified by its `value` and marked with a check while chosen.
typical_uses: One entry of a combobox's list, rendered for one item of the root's `items`

dont_use_when.situation: An entry that runs a command rather than setting a value

invariants.text: `value` is what choosing the item puts into the root's value; the root compares it with the chosen value by `Object.is` unless the root's `isItemEqualToValue` says otherwise.
While the item is chosen a check mark renders at its inline end; while it is not chosen the mark is not in the DOM.
A disabled item is still reached by arrow keys but cannot be chosen by pointer or keyboard, and combobox.module.css dims it and ignores pointer events on it.

anti_patterns.dont: Render the item as a `<button>` or another focusable element through `render`
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep the default div; focus stays on the field while the highlight moves through the items, and a focusable item takes it away

a11y.by: the primitive's Combobox.Item sets role="option" and aria-selected; combobox.test.tsx asserts the options are found by role option and that pressing the option named "Europe" reports "Europe" through onValueChange

children.states: children is the option's caption, any React content
children.because: `ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

value.states: value is the item this option stands for, of the caller's own item type
value.because: Typed `any` by the primitive, so the schema asserts nothing; it is one entry of the root's `items`.

onClick.states: onClick is a callback called when the item is pressed with the pointer, or with Enter while highlighted
onClick.because: A function of Base UI's wrapped mouse event, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the item's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the item's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled, selected, highlighted). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside ComboboxItem as the trailing check mark, styled by combobox.module.css.

good.title: An item rendered for one entry of the root's items

bad.title: An item with no value
bad.why: Without `value` the item stands for null, so in a one-value combobox choosing it sets the root's value to null, the same as clearing it; give every item the entry of `items` it renders.

children.description: Partially typed: ReactNode. The compiler emits one JSON type per property and none for this one; shape checked by tsc, see x-uikit.partially_typed_props. children is the option's caption, any React content. `ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

onClick.description: TS: ((event: BaseUIEvent<MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement, MouseEvent>>) => void) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. onClick is a callback called when the item is pressed with the pointer, or with Enter while highlighted. A function of Base UI's wrapped mouse event, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ComboboxItemState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the item's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: ComboboxItemState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the item's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled, selected, highlighted). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.

value.description: TS: any. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. value is the item this option stands for, of the caller's own item type. Typed `any` by the primitive, so the schema asserts nothing; it is one entry of the root's `items`.
